# sv-grid

> The Svelte 5-native data grid. Headless engine + render component, AI-native, WAI-ARIA, virtualized to 100k rows.

Two npm packages: `sv-grid-core` (MIT, open source) and `sv-grid-pro` (commercial - export, import, pivot, AI helpers).

For the full text of every doc page concatenated: see [llms-full.txt](/llms-full.txt).
For a machine-readable manifest: see [docs.json](/docs.json).

## Overview

- [Changelog](https://svgrid.com/changelog): The user-facing log of what shipped. Format follows Keep a Changelog 1.1.0; versioning follows Semantic Versioning.
- [Getting Started with SvGrid](https://svgrid.com/getting-started-full): SvGrid is a modern, production-ready data grid for Svelte 5 - a headless core engine paired with a Svelte render component (<SvGrid>). It scales from a 10-row read-only table to a virtualized 100,0…
- [Getting started with SvGrid](https://svgrid.com/getting-started): SvGrid is a modern, production-ready data grid for Svelte 5 - a headless core engine paired with a Svelte render component (<SvGrid>). It scales from a 10-row read-only table to a virtualized 100,0…
- [Why headless?](https://svgrid.com/why-headless): SvGrid is **headless at the core**, with a fully-styled Svelte component shipped on top. That two-layer split is deliberate, and worth understanding before you reach for either.

## Compliance

- [Audit log integration](https://svgrid.com/compliance/audit-log): A typed, tamper-evident audit trail of every user action in the grid, in under 50 lines. Pattern works for any backend - your existing audit table, Datadog logs, an immutable ledger (DynamoDB with …
- [GDPR + data residency](https://svgrid.com/compliance/gdpr): sv-grid is **GDPR-neutral**: the library never transmits personal data, never stores it server-side, and never logs it. If your app is GDPR-compliant before adding sv-grid, adding sv-grid does not …
- [HIPAA posture](https://svgrid.com/compliance/hipaa): sv-grid is **HIPAA-neutral**: the library does not transmit, store, or process PHI on its own. If your app is HIPAA-compliant before adding sv-grid, adding sv-grid does not break that compliance.
- [Compliance](https://svgrid.com/compliance/index): sv-grid is a client-side UI library - **all data stays in the browser**, the library never makes a network call of its own, no telemetry phones home. The compliance story is therefore short, but be…
- [SOC 2 posture](https://svgrid.com/compliance/soc2): sv-grid is a UI library, not a service - so it cannot itself hold a SOC 2 report. But it can sit inside a SOC 2-audited application, and the controls below describe the line where the library's res…

## Getting started

- [1. Install](https://svgrid.com/getting-started/1-install): SvGrid is a single npm package. There is no peer dependency on a CSS framework - bring your own, or use the default theme that ships with the render component.
- [2. First grid in 60 seconds](https://svgrid.com/getting-started/2-first-grid): ```svelte <script lang="ts"> import { SvGrid, type ColumnDef } from 'sv-grid-core'
- [3. Data and columns](https://svgrid.com/getting-started/3-data-and-columns): SvGrid reads two arrays: data (your rows) and columns (the column-definition list). Everything else is opt-in.
- [4. Features](https://svgrid.com/getting-started/4-features): The grid engine is **feature-gated**. Out of the box you get the core row model (rows in their original order). To enable sorting, filtering, grouping, pagination, expansion, or selection, register…
- [5. Theme and density](https://svgrid.com/getting-started/5-theme-and-density): The render component (<SvGrid>) ships its own scoped styles. You re-theme it by declaring --sg-* CSS custom properties at any level above the grid - :root for the whole app, a wrapper <div> for one…
- [6. Going to production](https://svgrid.com/getting-started/6-going-to-production): You have a working grid. This page is the checklist that turns it into something you'd ship.
- [Starters & scaffolding](https://svgrid.com/getting-started/starters): The fastest way to a working SvGrid app. One command scaffolds a project with the grid already wired up - no copy-paste, no config archaeology.

## Cells

- [Cell components](https://svgrid.com/help/cells/cell-components): For any cell whose content is more than a string, use cell: with renderSnippet or renderComponent. <div data-docs-demo="10-custom-cells-and-themes" data-height="540"></div>
- [Cell data types](https://svgrid.com/help/cells/cell-data-types): The editorType field on a column tags the column with a type. This drives three different behaviours: <div data-docs-demo="01-quick-start" data-height="540"></div>
- [Cell text selection](https://svgrid.com/help/cells/cell-text-selection): By default the grid has **cell-range selection** (drag across cells, range highlight, copy as TSV). Standard browser text-selection inside a cell is **not** the default - clicking-and-dragging acro…
- [Conditional formatting](https://svgrid.com/help/cells/conditional-formatting): Conditional formatting colors a cell by its value. SvGrid ships it as a declarative engine prop, conditionalFormats, so you describe the rules once and the grid paints every cell - no per-cell cell…
- [Expressions](https://svgrid.com/help/cells/expressions): SvGrid does not ship a formula / expression language for cells. Computed values are JavaScript - either via accessorFn or inside a cell callback. <div data-docs-demo="83-spreadsheet-formulas" data-…
- [Getting values](https://svgrid.com/help/cells/getting-values): You get cell values in three ways depending on context. <div data-docs-demo="04-selection-copy-paste" data-height="540"></div>
- [Highlighting changes](https://svgrid.com/help/cells/highlighting-changes): There is no built-in "flash on change" highlight. You build it with a diff against a frozen snapshot of the data. <div data-docs-demo="11-stock-market" data-height="540"></div>
- [Sparklines](https://svgrid.com/help/cells/sparklines): A sparkline is a tiny, word-sized chart drawn inside a single cell. SvGrid renders them as a first-class column type: set sparkline on a column whose value is an array of numbers and the grid paint…
- [Styling cells](https://svgrid.com/help/cells/styling-cells): Cells render as <td> and pick up the same CSS variable tokens as the rest of the grid. <div data-docs-demo="62-conditional-styling" data-height="540"></div>
- [Text formatting](https://svgrid.com/help/cells/text-formatting): The format field on a column produces locale-aware formatted strings without you writing a renderer. <div data-docs-demo="13-finances" data-height="540"></div>
- [Tooltips](https://svgrid.com/help/cells/tooltips): There is no built-in tooltip API on ColumnDef. Use the standard title attribute, an accessible <dialog>, or any popover library - wired through a custom cell renderer.
- [View refresh](https://svgrid.com/help/cells/view-refresh): The grid renders reactively - it does **not** have a refresh() method, because it doesn't need one. To make the grid re-display, change the data that drives it.

## Columns

- [Column definitions](https://svgrid.com/help/columns/column-definitions): A ColumnDef tells SvGrid how to read a value out of a row, how to render it, and which features apply to it. The grid below is built from a handful of ColumnDefs - look at the source to see how eac…
- [Column groups](https://svgrid.com/help/columns/column-groups): A column group is a ColumnDef whose columns array contains children. The parent renders a spanning header above its children. The pivot demo below shows three levels of grouped headers in action - …
- [Column headers - styling & height](https://svgrid.com/help/columns/column-headers): Headers are rendered as <th> inside a <thead> with role="row". Style them with regular CSS - there are no header-specific Svelte props. <div data-docs-demo="01-quick-start" data-height="540"></div>
- [Column moving (drag to reorder)](https://svgrid.com/help/columns/column-moving): There are two ways to move columns in sv-grid:
- [Column pinning](https://svgrid.com/help/columns/column-pinning): Pinning sticks a column to the **left** or **right** edge of the viewport so it does not scroll horizontally with the rest.
- [Column sizing](https://svgrid.com/help/columns/column-sizing): Each column has a pixel width. The default for all columns is the grid's columnWidth prop (default ~140 px); each column can override via its width field. <div data-docs-demo="63-column-layout-api"…
- [Column spanning](https://svgrid.com/help/columns/column-spanning): "Column spanning" lets a single body cell span across **multiple columns** - useful for full-width subtotals, group banner rows, or notes embedded inside a wide grid.
- [Column state](https://svgrid.com/help/columns/column-state): "Column state" is the bag of per-column settings that change at runtime: visibility, width, pinning, sort, filter. SvGrid keeps these as separate state slices inside the grid instance. <div data-do…
- [Custom header components](https://svgrid.com/help/columns/custom-header-components): The header field on a ColumnDef accepts a function that returns either a renderSnippet(...) or renderComponent(...). The function receives a HeaderContext so it can access the column, header, and g…
- [Columns tool panel](https://svgrid.com/help/columns/tool-panel): The tool panel is the docked sidebar - standard in enterprise grids - for managing columns without hunting through a right-click menu. Turn it on with the toolPanel prop:
- [Updating column definitions](https://svgrid.com/help/columns/updating-definitions): There are two ways to change columns after the grid has mounted:

## Editing

- [Edit components](https://svgrid.com/help/editing/edit-components): The grid ships with five inline editors. Each is selected by the column's editorType: <div data-docs-demo="66-custom-cell-editors" data-height="540"></div>
- [Full-row editing](https://svgrid.com/help/editing/full-row): "Full-row editing" means the user opens an entire row for edit (every editable cell becomes an editor simultaneously) and commits all changes at once. <div data-docs-demo="40-forms-master-detail" d…
- [Editing - overview](https://svgrid.com/help/editing/overview): Inline editing is a single prop on <SvGrid>. Try it - double-click any cell, type to replace, hit Enter to commit. Tab moves to the next editable cell:
- [Parsing values](https://svgrid.com/help/editing/parsing-values): When the user commits an edit, the editor's DOM value (a string for text / number / date inputs, a boolean for checkboxes) is parsed by parseEditorValue into the canonical value for the column's ty…
- [Provided cell editors](https://svgrid.com/help/editing/provided-editors): The grid ships nine built-in editors, selected via editorType on the column definition. Each editor renders inside the cell while editing and falls back to the default text render (or your cell sni…
- [Saving values](https://svgrid.com/help/editing/saving-values): When the user commits an edit, the new value is written into the grid's **internal data copy**. The grid does **not** mutate the array you passed in via the data prop - it keeps its own working cop…
- [Start / stop editing](https://svgrid.com/help/editing/start-stop-editing): The cell must be **focused** (the grid's active cell). Click any cell or use the arrow keys to set focus.
- [Undo / redo](https://svgrid.com/help/editing/undo-redo): There is **no built-in undo/redo stack** inside <SvGrid>. The grid emits no per-edit event for an external stack to subscribe to, so undo/redo has to be built on top of the data-snapshot approach. …
- [Validation](https://svgrid.com/help/editing/validation): There is no validate(value) callback on ColumnDef today. Validation happens by intercepting committed edits and either accepting or reverting them.

## Filtering

- [Applying filters](https://svgrid.com/help/filtering/applying-filters): "Applying" a filter means running it against the data. SvGrid applies filters **eagerly** by default: every keystroke updates the row model and the visible rows (with a 150ms debounce inside the co…
- [Custom column filters](https://svgrid.com/help/filtering/custom-column-filters): When the built-in operators and the set-filter pattern are not enough, take over the filter pipeline. <div data-docs-demo="03-excel-filters" data-height="540"></div>
- [Date filter](https://svgrid.com/help/filtering/date-filter): A column with editorType: 'date' (or 'datetime') gets the **date** filter operator set: equals, lessThan, greaterThan, **between**, isBlank. <div data-docs-demo="64-filter-between-operator" data-he…
- [Filter API](https://svgrid.com/help/filtering/filter-api): Two surfaces - pick based on whether the caller is inside or outside the component that owns the grid state. <div data-docs-demo="64-filter-between-operator" data-height="540"></div>
- [Filter conditions](https://svgrid.com/help/filtering/filter-conditions): A "filter condition" is a (column, operator, value) triple. The grid stores filter conditions in state.columnFilters. <div data-docs-demo="03-excel-filters" data-height="540"></div>
- [Floating filters](https://svgrid.com/help/filtering/floating-filters): "Floating filters" are the always-visible filter inputs that sit **between** the header row and the body - same idea as a filter row, but matched per-operator to the underlying column menu. <div da…
- [Number filter](https://svgrid.com/help/filtering/number-filter): A column with editorType: 'number' gets the **number** filter operator set: equals, greaterThan, lessThan, **between**, isBlank. The default operator is equals. <div data-docs-demo="64-filter-betwe…
- [Filtering - overview](https://svgrid.com/help/filtering/overview): Click any column header's filter icon to open the operator + value popover; numeric and date columns range-bucket their distinct values so the menu stays usable on big datasets:
- [Set filter](https://svgrid.com/help/filtering/set-filter): A "set filter" (a.k.a. value filter, list filter) shows a checklist of all distinct values in a column and lets the user pick which to include. It's what you reach for to filter status to "active O…
- [Text filter](https://svgrid.com/help/filtering/text-filter): A column with no editorType (or editorType: 'text') gets the **text** filter operator set: contains, equals, startsWith, isBlank. The default operator is contains. <div data-docs-demo="69-highlight…

## Rows

- [Accessing rows](https://svgrid.com/help/rows/accessing-rows): You can read the grid's current rows in three ways. <div data-docs-demo="04-selection-copy-paste" data-height="540"></div>
- [Full-width rows](https://svgrid.com/help/rows/full-width-rows): "Full-width rows" are rows whose content takes the entire grid width instead of being cell-by-cell - useful for inline editors, banner ads, section dividers, and detail-row expansions. <div data-do…
- [Row data](https://svgrid.com/help/rows/row-data): Row data is whatever you pass to <SvGrid data={...}>. It is a ReadonlyArray<TData> where TData is your row type. Any shape works; the grid does not require a base class or interface. <div data-docs…
- [Row dragging](https://svgrid.com/help/rows/row-dragging): Drag-to-reorder for rows is a common interaction (kanban-like reordering, moving items between two grids, dragging rows out to an external drop zone). <div data-docs-demo="23-bulk-actions" data-hei…
- [Row height](https://svgrid.com/help/rows/row-height): Row height is a single integer in pixels. <div data-docs-demo="10-custom-cells-and-themes" data-height="540"></div>
- [Row pagination](https://svgrid.com/help/rows/row-pagination): Pagination is opt-in. Register the feature, register the row model, then either turn it on with showPagination or drive its state from outside. <div data-docs-demo="02-sort-filter-paginate" data-he…
- [Row pinning (top / bottom)](https://svgrid.com/help/rows/row-pinning): Pin specific rows to the **top** or **bottom** of the grid so they stay visible while the rest of the data scrolls. Typical use cases:
- [Row sorting](https://svgrid.com/help/rows/row-sorting): Sorting is a feature you opt into. Try it live - click any column header to cycle none → asc → desc → none; shift-click adds the column to the sort key list (multi-sort):
- [Row spanning](https://svgrid.com/help/rows/row-spanning): "Row spanning" lets one cell's content cover **multiple rows**, the way a merged cell does in a spreadsheet.
- [Styling rows](https://svgrid.com/help/rows/styling-rows): Rows are <tr role="row"> elements inside the grid table. Style them with plain CSS. <div data-docs-demo="62-conditional-styling" data-height="540"></div>
- [Transactions](https://svgrid.com/help/rows/transactions): api.applyTransaction({ add, update, remove }) applies a batch of row mutations in a **single** data update - one re-render for the whole batch, not one per row. It's the path to use for high-freque…
- [Tree rows (expand / collapse)](https://svgrid.com/help/rows/tree-rows): SvGrid does not have a treeData prop. Tree-shaped data renders through the same data + columns pipeline as any other grid, with the tree behaviour living in *your* derived-state code. This is on pu…

## Pro tier

- [Pro evaluation](https://svgrid.com/pro/evaluation): The sv-grid-pro package is soft-gated; you can evaluate every feature in production-equivalent code paths without contacting sales. This page is the playbook.
- [Pro licensing](https://svgrid.com/pro/licensing): The sv-grid-pro package is **soft-gated**: every feature runs without a key, with a small unlicensed-build watermark in the bottom-right corner of the grid + a one-time console nudge. Set a key onc…
- [Pro feature pack](https://svgrid.com/pro/README): sv-grid-pro is a paid add-on for sv-grid-core. It bolts onto the same <SvGrid> you already have and adds four feature areas: data export, data import, an AI assistant, and pivot tables.
- [Pro support](https://svgrid.com/pro/support): What you get on each tier, what response time to expect, how to escalate.

- [Sparkline cell renderer](https://svgrid.com/recipes/sparkline-cells): In-cell mini-charts of a value series, rendered via inline SVG.
- [Submit-time validation with error summary](https://svgrid.com/recipes/submit-time-validation): Different from per-keystroke validation. The user edits freely; on **Submit**, a row-level validator runs and highlights every invalid cell with an aria-live summary panel.

- [Theme tokens for Ant / MUI / Fluent / shadcn](https://svgrid.com/recipes/theme-presets): Map your design system's tokens to --sg-* and the grid re-skins.
- [Two-grid master / detail](https://svgrid.com/recipes/two-grid-master-detail): Goal: one grid shows the **master** (parents - orders, customers, projects, …), a second grid below shows the **detail** for whichever row is selected (line items, contacts, tasks, …).
- [Undo / redo for grid edits](https://svgrid.com/recipes/undo-redo-edits): Maintain a history stack of cell edits; Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y replay backwards / forwards.

- [WebSocket streaming with backpressure](https://svgrid.com/recipes/websocket-streaming): Live tick stream with pause / resume / disconnect-and-replay and per-tick delta merge.

- [`ColumnDef` reference](https://svgrid.com/reference/ColumnDef): A column definition is the contract between the grid and one column of data. Pass an array of these as the columns prop to <SvGrid>.
- [Features reference](https://svgrid.com/reference/features): A "feature" is a small bundle of state + helpers the grid engine checks for when wiring its row-model pipeline. Register only what you use - each feature ships about 1-2 KB gzipped and adds a small…
- [Headless engine](https://svgrid.com/reference/headless-engine): createSvGrid(options) returns a table object with:
- [API reference](https://svgrid.com/reference/index): The exhaustive surface of the published packages. For walkthroughs + patterns see Help; for first contact see Getting started.
- [Pro reference](https://svgrid.com/reference/pro): Everything that sv-grid-pro adds on top of the Community surface. Install + license: see Pro feature pack.
- [`<SvGrid>` reference](https://svgrid.com/reference/SvGrid): The render component. One <SvGrid> element per grid instance.
- [`SvGridApi` reference](https://svgrid.com/reference/SvGridApi): The imperative API exposed via <SvGrid onApiReady={(api) => ...}>. Use it for data, column, filter, sort, group, selection, and visibility operations from outside the component.
